hints: Notice $n$ is defined as number density of free electrons, meaning number per unit volume with unit $\text{m}^{-3}$, not number per unit area.
Picture the electrons that flow past a point in time $t$ as a cylinder of length $vt$ and cross-sectional area $A$, so its volume is $Avt$.
Track how total number $N$ must combine $n$ with that cylinder volume, then with $q$ and $t$, to see which stated product with area alone never appears.
walkthrough: Consider a length $l$ of wire that is swept past a point by electrons of drift speed $v$ in time $t$.
The distance moved is $l = vt$ using distance = speed $\times$ time.
The swept-out region is a cylinder of volume $V = Al = Avt$ using volume = length $\times$ area.
The number of free electrons in it is $N = nV = nAvt$ because $n$ is number per unit volume.
Their total charge is $Q = Nq = nAvtq$ and current is $I = Q/t = nAvq$ using charge = current $\times$ time.
The derivation therefore needs number = number density $\times$ volume, not number = number density $\times$ area. This is option C

options.A: This is used as $I = Q/t$, so total charge $Q$ passing in time $t$ gives the current.
options.B: This is used as $l = vt$ for the length of wire emptied of electrons in time $t$.
options.C: Number density $n$ is number per unit volume, so number is $n$ times volume $nAl$, not $n$ times area alone.
options.D: This is used as $V = Al$ for the volume of the cylinder of electrons that passes in time $t$.
